name_note: GTDB divides Akkermansia muciniphila into several species-level lineages and marks this one _A; the papers and NCBI use the undivided name Akkermansia muciniphila.

sentences.text: Akkermansia muciniphila is a commensal bacterium that represents 1 to 4 percent of the fecal microbiota in healthy adults and can use mucin as a sole source of carbon and nitrogen.

A review discusses evidence that Akkermansia muciniphila and specific bacterial proteins stimulate the proliferation and differentiation of intestinal stem cells, as part of tissue homeostasis and repair after injury.
Large phylogenetic and functional diversity within the Akkermansia genus has prompted comparisons of different strains for their individual health profiles.
Longitudinal metagenomic data from 7 healthy individuals showed significant fluctuations in its relative abundance, including short-term blooms.
In the same analysis, closely related strains were shared between cohabiting subjects and across China, South Korea and the United States.
